## Context / Problem

ADR 0122 fixed the retrieval architecture but left the index unbuilt. This story builds it on a tier needing no model provider, credentials or network, so retrieval works everywhere. Siblings add embedding ranking, the create advisory and the ADR amendments.

## Approach

### Ranking

sqlite FTS5 over title and description, bm25 weights title 5.0 / description 1.0 — ADR 0122's measured `fts5` baseline (`evals/similar-tickets/measure.py:389-396`, weights `"0.0, 5.0, 1.0"`). Semantic recall@5 0.823 vs the adopted `vector`'s 0.876; it wins at lexical recall@10 (0.993 vs 0.972, p=0.0000) — ADR 0122's reason for keeping it. Query text is title plus description's first 200 characters, per ADR 0122.

Results cap at 5: ADR 0122's decision is scoped to k=5, and at k=10 `vector`'s edge is indistinguishable (p=0.3438), so the evidence favours building nothing. Another count invalidates the comparison.

The query API excludes a caller-supplied ticket id: a create queries with its own text, already indexed by catch-up, so without the exclusion it returns itself as top match.

`id`, `alias` and `title` are stored index columns, so a query needs no ticket-store read. `score` is computed per query and normalized to 0–1, 1 most relevant: raw bm25 is negative and ranks ascending, which inverts the conventional reading and leaves consumers unable to assert on it.

### Persistence and freshness

A sqlite file under `.rebar/cache/similar-tickets/`, mirroring the git-ignored `.rebar/cache/plan-review/` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/checkpoints.py:33-37`). `.gitignore:23` ignores `.rebar/*` wholesale, so no ignore change is needed and nothing derived reaches `tickets`.

The index persists a map from ticket directory to its last-indexed directory mtime **and** dir hash, which makes catch-up cheap and new tickets discoverable. `compute_dir_hash(ticket_dir, event_filenames)` (`src/rebar/reducer/_cache.py:122`) supplies the per-directory hash only — it detects change in a known directory but cannot discover a new one. Catch-up therefore runs two steps:

1. **Enumerate** the live ticket-directory set from the store.
2. **Diff** it against the persisted map, in two levels: an unchanged directory mtime means skip, with no `listdir` and no hashing; only a directory whose mtime moved is hashed, and the **hash — not the mtime — decides**. No entry means new, so index it; a differing hash means changed, so re-index it; a missing directory means gone, so drop the entry.

Catch-up is synchronous, in the read phase before serving a query — no daemon, background thread or CI trigger — so behaviour is identical on a fresh clone, under MCP, and where no CI provider exists.

### Applying the diff

The diff is applied **in place, to the live index, inside one sqlite transaction** — never built into a replacement database. Unchanged entries survive by construction: reconciliation touches only the rows the diff named. A fresh database built from the diff alone would discard every entry it did not name; copying the live file first would pay the store's full size on every create.

sqlite supplies the atomicity and crash-safety, so no temporary file and no `os.rename` swap appears — neither call is used, so their POSIX/Windows overwrite difference cannot arise. The index opens WAL with a busy timeout and wraps each reconciliation in `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` … `COMMIT`. An interrupted process rolls back to the previous committed state, and concurrent reconcilers serialize on sqlite's write lock, a loser's work redone rather than merged since each recomputes its hashes. A corrupt index is discarded and rebuilt, so the cache is regenerable and needs no eviction path.

On an unchanged store every mtime matches its stored value, so the diff is empty, no transaction opens and no FTS5 write occurs: warm cost is one enumeration plus **one stat per ticket directory**. Per-*file* statting was measured and rejected — the cost is the event-file count, not the call shape, so it misses the warm budget; one stat per directory is ~95x cheaper on this store. The implemented warm path measures a p95 of 111 ms over 20 runs.

The mtime never decides — it only permits skipping the exact hash check — and is read before the content, so a concurrent write at worst causes redundant re-hashing, never a missed change. Measurements, and why the pre-filter is sound for an append-only store: see the ticket comment.

### Failure disposition

Every failure path returns an empty result rather than raising, so retrieval can never fail a caller. Each swallowed failure logs at warning level first; without it a corrupt index degrades to permanently empty results with no symptom.

No new config key is added; any ratcheted mechanism carries a `# mechanism-ok:` marker naming this ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A query ranks by sqlite FTS5 bm25 with title weighted 5.0 and description 1.0. Checked by: a test asserting the weights.
- [ ] A query returns at most 5 results. Checked by: a test over a store with more matches.
- [ ] Each result carries `id`, `alias`, `title` and `score`. Checked by: a shape test on one result.
- [ ] Every `score` lies in the closed interval 0 to 1. Checked by: a test asserting the range.
- [ ] The top-ranked result holds the maximum `score` of the set. Checked by: a test asserting the ordering.
- [ ] A caller-supplied excluded ticket id never appears in that query's results. Checked by: a test querying a ticket's own text and id.
- [ ] Catch-up indexes a ticket directory created after the last build. Checked by: a test creating one, running catch-up, then querying.
- [ ] Catch-up drops entries whose ticket directory no longer exists. Checked by: a test removing one then querying.
- [ ] Catch-up re-indexes a ticket whose dir hash changed. Checked by: a test mutating one then matching its updated text.
- [ ] Reconciling a diff naming one ticket leaves every other indexed ticket returnable with its prior text. Checked by: a test indexing 3, mutating 1, asserting the others unchanged.
- [ ] Catch-up performs no re-indexing work on an unchanged store. Checked by: a test asserting the re-indexed count is 0 on a second run.
- [ ] A warm query completes within a p95 of 500 ms over at least 20 runs. Checked by: a timing test over a synthetic store it generates.
- [ ] That timing test asserts its store holds at least 10,000 tickets before measuring. Checked by: its precondition assertion.
- [ ] The cold-catch-up p95 over that store is emitted as a numeric figure. Checked by: a test asserting it is produced.
- [ ] A ticket created in-process is returned by the next query in that process, with no daemon, background thread, MCP server or CI. Checked by: an integration test.
- [ ] With every model-provider credential environment variable unset, a query returns a non-empty ranked result. Checked by: an integration test clearing them.
- [ ] After 100 writes and 100 queries against a test store, the `tickets` branch holds only user event types. Checked by: an integration test asserting that set.
- [ ] A query returns an empty result rather than raising both when the index file is absent and when catch-up raises. Checked by: a test for each source.
- [ ] A corrupt index file is discarded, rebuilt, and a query against the rebuilt index returns results. Checked by: a test corrupting it then querying.
- [ ] The absent-index, corrupt-index and raising-catch-up paths each emit a warning-level log record. Checked by: a test capturing logs on each.
- [ ] After two concurrent catch-up runs the index passes `PRAGMA integrity_check` and both tickets written are returnable. Checked by: a test running two in parallel then querying each.
- [ ] Every module added or modified under `src/rebar/` is at most 800 lines. Checked by: the CI module-size gate.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exits 0. Checked by: running it.
